v1.feedback: The wake-ring radiating outward to raise submerged Voronoi buildings is a legible read on 'wake' and clearly descends from the parent's speculative-topography grid — good lineage. However the buildings are wireframe boxes with near-invisible 0.15 opacity, so the city never feels substantial; bump opacity to 0.4–0.6 and add a subtle emissive fill so the risen structures read as solid mass. The water shader's warm ring is nice but the vast dark plane around it wastes most of the canvas — tighten the camera FOV or pull it closer so particles occupy more frame area. Courier V-wake trails are a smart touch but their additive blending washes out against the dark water; consider a brighter accent or a second cooler tone to separate boat-wakes from the ring wake.

v2.feedback: The dual 'wake' reading (awakening + water-wake) is genuinely clever and the radial rise mechanic makes the chain lineage legible — you can feel the speculative-topography parent underneath. Two problems: the lime-green ring color (0xa0ff3c) clashes hard with the dark-blue/cyan palette; swap it for a cooler cyan or desaturated teal so the wake ring doesn't read as a UI element. The buildings are plain BoxGeometry wireframes — even slight per-building width/depth aspect variation or a tapered top would sell 'city' faster at the 30° FOV framing. Consider fading the street-graph lines *in* behind the wake ring rather than rendering them at full extent from frame one, so the reveal has a single focal moment instead of competing layers.
